elements.title: Audubon Terrace (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that New York City's Audubon Terrace (pictured) was so poorly patronized that one of its museums once lent items to another museum in the city so more people could see them?

elements.title: Henri Gil-Marchex (Wikipedia — did you know?)

elements.title: court-ordered integration of a public school (Wikipedia — did you know?)

elements.title: Dániel Karsai (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Dániel Karsai worked at the European Court of Human Rights, the same court that later ruled against him by not decriminalizing euthanasia?

elements.title: a parallel local government (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that a parallel local government operated independently of British rule in Medinipur during the 1942 Quit India Movement?

elements.title: a cultivar of crape myrtle (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that a cultivar of crape myrtle was named after a video-game character because its flowers resemble her hair bow?

elements.title: clippable (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that some studios and streaming platforms have reportedly begun instructing filmmakers to film TV shows and films in a manner that can make them easily clippable?

elements.title: Ana Paula Gomes de Oliveira (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Ana Paula Gomes de Oliveira won the Martin Ennals Award for Human Rights Defenders after campaigning against police brutality in Brazil following the death of her son?

elements.title: Lady of Lawers (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the Lady of Lawers was said to have foreseen the Highland Clearances via a prophecy about sheep skulls and ploughs?
